record.prBody:
## 27 changes: stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed and more [Not affected]

### Change

No code changes. The repo is on stripe 22.0.0 and already uses `new Stripe(key)` at server.js:15. I ran `require('stripe')` under Node 22 in the sandbox. It returns a constructor, and `new S('sk_test_x')` constructs without error. The calls to checkout.sessions.create and retrieve, billingPortal.sessions.create and webhooks.constructEvent use no removed API. There is no per-request host override, no apiVersion override, no constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType, parseThinEvent or ui_mode, and no decimal_string fields. All 27 listed changes need no change: item 1 (v22) is satisfied, and the rest cover Python, Go or Stripe.js, or API and SDK versions the repo does not use. The Python and Go items don't apply because the repo is plain JS. Upcoming, not acted on: if the repo later moves to stripe-node 23 (API 2026-09-30.endive), `payment_method_types: ['card']` at server.js:291 on checkout.sessions.create must be removed. Node 20 support ends in the September 2027 major.

No files changed.

### Why

The v22 breaking change is that the default export is a true class, so it must be built with `new`. The repo already does that, and it pins ^22.0.0. The other listed changes don't touch the Stripe calls it makes.

> Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

No checks were run.

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The repo has no tests, build or typecheck scripts, so no checks were registered.
- Stripe calls were not exercised, and no provider validator was run.
- Upgrading to stripe-node 23 and API version endive is not covered. Removing `payment_method_types` would be needed then.
- No checks were run.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.

---

## 6 changes: @upstash/redis (npm) 1.40.0 defaults responseEncoding to false (plain JSON strings); behaviour changes for BOM, binary data, abort() results and more [Not affected]

### Change

No code changed. The repo uses @upstash/redis (^1.37.0, installed 1.37.0) only for single get/set/incr/expire calls in server.js. The values are plain strings, numbers, and JSON objects. It does not use auto-pipelining, pipeline/multi, readYourWrites, or responseEncoding. The @upstash/ratelimit package is not a dependency, and the 'ratelimit' strings in server.js are only Redis key prefixes for a hand-written limiter. The Promise.all calls in scripts/generate-seo-content.js do not involve Redis.

No files changed.

### Why

1) responseEncoding default false: the SDK decodes responses itself, so callers still get the same values. Neither the client option nor the base64 encoding is referenced anywhere in the repo. 2) Auto-pipeline split (1.38.0): no pipelining is used. 3) readYourWrites sync-token fix (1.38.4): this is internal to the SDK and needs no code change. 4–6) The @upstash/ratelimit changes (tokenBucket, getRemaining, cacheScripts): the package is not used.
